claims.text: A Bayesian uncertainty-quantification-enhanced hybrid analytical-numerical model will reduce uncertainty in conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen relative to traditional perfect-crystal analytical approaches.
The model will accurately capture the effects of oxygen-induced defects and microstructural disorder on conductivity over the nearly 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The 1 wt.% oxygen specimen has a realistic defect landscape comprising point defects, defect clusters, and local lattice distortions observed experimentally.
Conductivity in the 0–200 K regime is dominated by quantum and static-defect effects.
Conductivity in the 300–1200 K regime is governed by phonon scattering and dynamic-defect effects.
Oxygen-induced local lattice distortions, point-defect concentrations, and clustering modify electronic band structure and scattering rates.
Bayesian calibration against experimental data can constrain uncertain defect, band-structure, and scattering parameters.
Learning effective corrections from experimental data will overcome errors caused by pristine, defect-free assumptions and improve conductivity-prediction accuracy and reliability.
The model's conductivity prediction at 600 K will be within ±10% of the measured conductivity.
The model will predict nonlinear temperature dependence with distinct low- and high-temperature trends.
The proposed model will outperform traditional models that neglect defect effects.
Existing analytical approaches generally assume defect-free crystals and neglect oxygen impurities.
Existing analytical approaches exhibit larger error bars and systematic deviations from experimental conductivity in both specified temperature regimes.
The calibrated model is applicable only within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K and when defect characteristics are well defined.
Extrapolation outside the calibration temperature windows may introduce significant uncertainty.
Predictive accuracy may be limited by the availability and quality of defect-state data and by unmodeled interactions at temperature extremes.
Static-defect scattering dominates low-temperature behavior, whereas dynamic defect clustering influences high-temperature conductivity.

contradictions.description: The model is said to be calibrated against available conductivity data throughout 300–1200 K, which includes 600 K, while the 600 K measurement is also proposed as the falsification benchmark. No explicit exclusion of the 600 K datum from calibration is specified, so the benchmark is not demonstrably held out.
